confirmed.statement: The paper reports one study with 60 people. The abstract says 'Through a between-participants experiment (N=60)'. Section 3.2 says 'We recruited 60 participants through digital student notice boards, mailing lists of university student clubs, and word of mouth.' The form's quote is verbatim and its locator is right.

All 60 were randomized, 20 per arm. 'After completing the questionnaire, the participants were randomly assigned to one of the three conditions' and 'Each condition had an equal number of participants and was gender-balanced, with 10 women and 10 men per condition'. This supports study n_randomized 60 and arm n_randomized 20, 20, 20.

The counts are people. Each person took part in one individual session ('Participants booked a time to participate individually'). Sketches (277), prompts (117), and AI images (468) appear only as outcome units or descriptive counts, never as participant counts.
confirmed.locator: p. 6, Section 3.3; p. 5, Section 3.1; pp. 11-12, Sections 4.6.1-4.6.2

confirmed.statement: No person is lost between randomization and analysis. I read PDF pp. 1-18 and searched the text for exclusion, removal, dropout, withdrawal, replacement, attrition, pilot, missing, and outlier terms. The only removal is of 10 GenAI sketches drawn before any prompt, from the within-GenAI correlation (82 of 92 sketches). It removes sketches, not people, and does not touch the outcome models. Screening of applicants came before recruitment and assignment. The form's 'None reported' is right.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 1-18; p. 12, Section 4.6.2; p. 5, Section 3.2

confirmed.statement: The analyses cover every participant. 'Each participant received a Variety score', fluency counts the sketches 'produced by each participant', and all 277 sketches were clustered. The NASA-TLX one-way ANOVA reports F(2, 57) = 1, p = 0.37, which implies 60 people (57 + 3 groups). Checker arithmetic gives p = 0.374.

The GenAI arm has 20 analyzed people. 'a total of 117 prompts, with a mean of 5.85 prompts per participant' gives 117 / 5.85 = 20.0. The range of 2 to 15 prompts means every GenAI participant used Midjourney. 117 prompts times four images gives the 468 AI images reported later.
confirmed.locator: p. 11, Section 4.6.1; p. 12, Section 4.6.2; p. 4, Section 3.1

confirmed.statement: Tables 1-4 and Figures 6-9 print no N for any outcome model, as the form says. So n_analyzed 60 and 20 per arm rest on the per-participant scoring statements, F(2, 57), the GenAI prompt count, and the absence of any reported loss, not on a printed model N.

Checker arithmetic, an inference: the Table 2 total-effect coefficients give model means of 4.48, 2.75, and 3.63 sketches per person. At 20 per arm they sum to 217.2 (215.5 to 218.9 with rounding), which is 59.8 short of the 277 sketches. 92 GenAI sketches / 20 = 4.6 = 3.63 + 1. The printed totals fit 20 people per arm if each person has one sketch that the fluency model does not count. Under the literal reading of Eq. 2, no split of 60 people fits: 92 GenAI sketches would need 25 people. The text does not explain this gap, which is a question for the outcome lens, not for the people counts.
confirmed.locator: p. 5, Eq. 2 and 'N=277'; p. 9, Table 2 and Figure 7; p. 12, '92 in total'

confirmed.statement: The paper does not say how exactly 10 women and 10 men reached each condition. With 30 women and 30 men split at random into three fixed arms of 20, every arm gets 10 women about 5 percent of the time (checker arithmetic, 0.053). Assignment was probably stratified by gender. This bears on how people were assigned, not on how many, and the form records the gap.

No shared sample. The paper reports one study and cites no earlier use of its participants. arXiv 2403.11164 has only v1 (17 Mar 2024), the copy on file, with N=60 in the abstract. The only other record by the first author in candidates.json, c605 (Wadinambiarachchi, Waycott, Wadley 2026), is a new within-participants study of the SketchifAI prototype, and its abstract mentions no reuse of participants or data. de Rooij and Biskjaer (2026) is a meta-analysis that includes this study, not a second sample.
confirmed.locator: whole PDF; candidates.json records c127 and c605; arxiv.org/abs/2403.11164; arxiv.org/abs/2606.26626

confirmed.statement: The other participant fields match the text: adults 18 or older with self-described visual-design experience; mean age 25.8 (18-49, SD 5.4); undergraduate, master's, and PhD students from arts, business, computer science and IT, design, engineering, and science; 'few had professional industry experience'; 'novice designers'. Population 'students' rests on the student recruitment channels and 'They included undergraduate, master’s and PhD students'. 'Included' and word-of-mouth recruitment leave room for some non-students. The paper names no country, and the lab and ethics sentences are as the form quotes them.
confirmed.locator: p. 5, Section 3.2; p. 16, Sections 5.4 and 6; p. 3, Section 3; p. 6, Section 3.3; p. 1, affiliations

confirmed.statement: The arm descriptions match the text: paid Midjourney V4 through a private Discord server, four images per prompt; Google Images in an incognito browser; Baseline 'no inspiration support'. The two tool arms got a video tutorial. All arms got the same brief, example avatar, drawing materials, and 20 minutes.
Criterion 2 holds for this one study: 60 people analyzed across three arms of 20. The GenAI versus no-support contrast alone has 40.

summary: The source supports every participant count in the form: 60 recruited people were randomly assigned to three conditions of 20 (10 women and 10 men each), the text reports no exclusion or loss of any person, and F(2, 57), per-participant scoring, and 117 prompts at 5.85 per GenAI participant confirm 60 analyzed and 20 per arm. No outcome model prints its N and the paper does not explain the exact gender balance, but the single study of 60 people meets the 50-person criterion and shares no participants with another paper.
